text:
alex: Heads up — ran a short repro on the 2k-token perf test and saw a clear regression after the cuda-graph+kv-prefetch change.  p50 ~1% better but p99 is ~18% worse. attaching quick profiler dump and notes.

maria: ugh. do you have a flamegraph or nvprof snapshot?

alex: nvprof capture (trimmed):
```
Host: request 0 -> launch graph on stream A
GPU: async memcpy H2D (stream B) [kv prefetch]
GPU: kernel compute (stream A)
GPU: NCCL all-reduce (stream C)
GPU: kernel compute continuation (stream A)
```
Looks like the H2D memcpy on stream B is suddenly blocking compute on stream A during graph replay. nvtx shows cudaGraphLaunch may be binding streams and forcing serialization. p99 jumps when kv hits (so it's data-dependent).

kevin: Interesting — I remember a similar pattern with stream capture where cudaGraph replays reuse stream exec context and that can interact badly with peer-to-peer memcpys or non-captured async memcpy streams. Any chance the graph capture included a stream barrier by accident?

alex: I dug in: the graph we generate captures the model kernels and the NCCL ops, but KV prefetch uses a separate stream (we expected it to overlap). After the change, graph replay seems to implicitly synchronize that prefetch in some cases. Reproducer attached: `runtime/tests/repro/graph-kv-overlap.py` (simple single-batch, multi-gpu).

jamie: Can you paste the minimal snippet of how you create streams and capture? maybe we accidentally used the same stream handle for capture and prefetch on some code path.

alex: snippet:
```
stream_compute = cuda.Stream()
stream_prefetch = cuda.Stream()
with cuda.graph_capture(stream_compute):
  model.forward(..., stream=stream_compute)
  nccl.allreduce(..., stream=nccl_stream)
# prefetch runs on stream_prefetch outside capture
kv.prefetch(keys, dst_stream=stream_prefetch)
cuda.graph_launch(captured)
```
Before change, prefetch overlapped. After patch X (change in kernel selection that also changed how we bind nccl stream handles into the captured graph) it stops overlapping.

maria: Do we set any stream dependencies for NCCL? A lot of our allreduce path creates an nccl communicator tied to a default stream; if that gets coalesced into the graph, it could impose ordering.

kevin: Also check if we set `cudaStreamAttachMemAsync` or use unified memory for kv buffers. Attachment semantics + graph replay can force implicit syncs.

alex: Confirmed: KV uses cudaMalloc + cudaMemcpyAsync into pinned buffer on stream_prefetch. No attach calls. But the k-selection change replaced a kernel that used a small inplace memcpy with a kernel that uses a cooperative async copy path which ended up being captured into the graph in some code paths. So we now have an extra memcpy inside the graph touching the same device memory region — could be implicit hazard.

jamie: Can we repro with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`? probably will hide overlap bugs but good for isolation.

kevin: I can repro locally on 4xA100, running your repro script. Profiling shows stream A waits on an event that is signaled by a cudaGraphLaunch which includes the memcpy node. So timeline: graph launch -> memcpy node (captured) -> event -> compute resumes. Graph captures seem to pull the previously independent prefetch into the ordering because of a memory alias.

alex: Workarounds: 1) pin KV prefetch to the same graph (capture it) — not ideal. 2) change kernel selection back for that path (fast rollback). 3) insert explicit `cudaEventRecord`/`cudaStreamWaitEvent` to force intended concurrency. 4) disable graph capture when KV prefetch is enabled.

maria: For short term, a rollback of the kernel change seems fastest. Can you bisect to the exact commit?

alex: will start bisect now. `git bisect start HEAD vX` then `git bisect run scripts/ci/perf_repro.sh`. results in ~30 commits to check.

kevin: I also want to try a micro patch: when we build the graph, use `cudaGraphInstantiate` with `cudaGraphNodeTypeKernel` params set to avoid reusing the stream? not sure if that is possible portably.

jamie: Another angle — update our KV prefetch to use device-to-device pinned staging and then a small kernel to copy inside the compute stream (so nothing external). That guarantees no cross-stream dependencies, but is a perf tradeoff.

infra-bot: deploy:perf: run queued - job perf/graph-kv-overlap/1849123456 started by alex

kevin: Also check NCCL async modes: we sometimes create nccl operations on a dedicated stream and then call `ncclCommEnqueue` with an implicit sync. If our kernel change moved where we create the communicator (inside capture), that would force ordering.

alex: Good catch — new kernel chooser moved `ncclCommCreate` to later in the pipeline to select a specialized kernel that requires communicator-specific params. That likely got captured.

maria: Plan: (1) revert kernel chooser commit in canary branch and run perf job, (2) create a targeted test exercising capture + external prefetch overlap, (3) add CI check (small flame/profiler) to catch regressions.

alex: I'll open the revert PR and attach the perf run. If the revert fixes p99, we can rework the kernel selection so it doesn't move communicator creation into capture region.

kevin: If you want I can prototype the explicit event-based workaround in a branch — if it reduces p99 without revert we can ship quicker.

alex: please do, thanks. tagging @maria @jamie for visibility. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — good triage. keep notes in the thread and paste bisect result when done.
